children: The National Oil Processors Association's report of a record 234.2 million bushels of soybeans crushed in October helps toward the USDA's target for the year, Mike Castle of StoneX says in a note. "The slow start to the 2026/27 marketing year after a weak September, amid earlier notable soybean harvest delays, had us in catch-up mode to reach USDA's record 2.78 billion-bushel crush target, and today's print certainly helps with that." At 430.5 million bushels in the first two months, the crush pace is 1.1% ahead of last year at this time, while the USDA looks for a 5.1% year-on-year increase, he notes. "With crush now accounting for over 60% of total U.S. soybean demand, this is an increasingly important metric to watch moving forward." Soybeans are off 0.6% on CBOT.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
